correctness.rationale: For every odd p, length-two ring has |m|=q and m^2=0. The p-element unipotent multiplier kernel and prime-to-p residue orders yield the exact lift counts. Nonidentity residue multipliers conjugate to scalar multiplication and give two disjoint cycle types. Radical translations give the p-cycle and q-fixed-point cases. Unit translations satisfy f^p(x)=x+pa; this is identity in char p and fixed-point-free nonzero translation in char p^2. Count categories sum to q^3(q-1), and actual independent enumerations for q=3,5,9 confirm all coefficients and fixed-point distributions. Computation is supplemental, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The all-finite-chain-ring conjugacy result is broader in underlying ring family, but class-size and character-degree spectra do not determine the cycle type of a natural permutation action. Its explicit conjugacy structure is relevant background but not an already-proved cycle-index count. The affine monoid centralizer paper has a broader monoid and counts centralizers, not permutation cycles. Affine Frobenius dynamics over fields excludes rings with square-zero radical.

originality.rationale: The classical cyclic prime-power affine cycle index is explicitly credited, not claimed new. The new uniform odd-prime-power residue-field comparison covers all f>=2, where split and Galois rings have identical fixed-point counts but an exactly distinguished p^2-cycle spectrum. Full text of the closest published affine-group conjugacy/character theorem and affine-monoid centralizer theorem describes different statistics, not natural permutation cycle types. A 2011 primary thesis covers q=p mixed-characteristic only. Equivalence through hidden classical formula remains a qualified residual risk.
residual_risks: Classical cycle-index formula for Aff(Z/p^a) covers the f=1 mixed-characteristic specialization, not claimed as new.
The 2019 affine-cycle-index repository PDF was not read after direct timeout; the indexed abstract appears limited to prime fields.
An unindexed prior formula for Aff(GR(p^2,f)) or dual-number affine groups, or a more general permutation cycle theorem, may exist.
Older group-conjugacy structure supplies many of the ingredients, so priority pertains only to the complete natural permutation-cycle comparison and its f>1 reconstruction.

value.rationale: The cycle index is a canonical complete natural-action statistic used to count colorings and orbits, not a contrived slice. It distinguishes two ring isomorphism types that have identical fixed-point distributions and previously established identical group conjugacy/character-degree spectra. The result is a uniform f>=2 extension of prime-cyclic work, covers entire group action, and cleanly identifies an arithmetic characteristic obstruction (p^2 cycles).
